title: VPC Edge Provisioner: subnet scaling strategies, NAT/IGW orchestration, and endpoint routing module
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build a production-ready Terraform module (and CI pipeline) that provisions VPC edge networking for Private deployments. The module must support: AZ-aware subnet allocation, deterministic public/private subnet tagging, multi-NAT/IGW orchestration with automatic failover, interface and gateway VPC endpoints with least-privilege policies, route table generation per AZ, and observability hooks for health-checking and upgrade safety.

Scope: 1) Core Terraform module (vpc-edge-provisioner) that creates: VPC, tiered subnets (control, app-private, app-public, egress), NAT Gateways (per-AZ with Elastic IP allocation), Internet Gateways, route tables, VPC endpoints (S3, STS, KMS, ECR, EC2, and customer-configurable endpoints), endpoint route propagation, and cross-account endpoint support. 2) Upgrade strategy and lifecycle: resource versioning, immutable subnet replacement pattern for AZ expansion, TF workspace branching strategy, provider pinning, and module version bump/upgrade playbook. 3) Health checks and smoke tests: periodic route table drift detection, NAT Gateway availability probe, Endpoint interface ENI status checks, FlowLog sampling tests, and a k8s-bootstrap smoke test for Private deployments. 4) CI/CD: terraform fmt/validate/plan in PR, automated drift detection in nightly runs, canary apply to a staging tenant, and automated rollback on failed post-apply smoke checks.

Design decisions and constraints: - Must support both single-account and cross-account Private installs (assume IAM role chaining for endpoint creation). - Default to per-AZ NAT Gateways for predictable egress latency but provide a \"single-nat\" toggle for cost-sensitive customers. - Subnet sizing uses deterministic CIDR allocator with per-tenant seed to avoid overlap; include optional secondary CIDR support for AZ expansion. - Endpoint policies generated from least-privilege templates, overridable by customer config. - Avoid stateful replacement of VPC-level resources where possible; document required manual steps for unavoidable replacements (e.g., switch IGW if changing route design).

Acceptance criteria: - Terraform module passes integration tests in the private-deploy staging account: VPC + 3 AZs provisioned, NAT failover tested (terminate NAT in AZ1 -> traffic routed through AZ2 NAT). - Auto-generated route tables include correct routes for endpoints and NAT/IGW. - Healthcheck lambda/pinger reports status and posts to ops Slack channel via webhook on any degraded resource. - CI pipeline blocks merge on plan failures and runs post-apply smoke checks before promoting to release staging.

Outputs and integration points: Outputs include vpc_id, subnet_ids by tier and AZ, nat_gateway_ids, igw_id, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids, and a JSON manifest used by downstream runtime provisioning. Module will be consumed by private-deploy bootstrap and by an internal \"tenant-provisioner\" service.

Documentation & artifacts: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Edge+Provisioner (draft). Terraform registry module page scaffold: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/tree/main/vpc-edge-provisioner (WIP). Integration test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-smoke-tests (contains the NAT failover script and endpoint ENI assertions).
